questions.question: A therapist designs an exercise program for a patient rehabilitating from a lower extremity injury. The single most important factor in an exercise program designed to increase muscular strength is:

options.A: The recovery time between exercise sets
options.B: The number of repetitions per set
options.C: The duration of the exercise session

questions.explanation: Exercise intensity (load) is the most important variable for increasing strength.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist implements an aquatic program for a patient rehabilitating from a total hip replacement. During the treatment session the patient indicates how much easier it is to walk in the water compared to on land. What factor is responsible for the patient's ability to walk in water?
questions.explanation: Buoyancy reduces weight bearing and makes walking in water easier.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist instructs a patient diagnosed with rotator cuff tendonitis in a home exercise program. The most important consideration when designing a home exercise program is to:

options.A: Focus the program on the individual needs of the patient
options.B: Limit the length of the program to 10 minutes
options.C: Provide written instructions that detail the frequency and duration of each exercise
options.D: Provide written instructions that detail the frequency and duration of each exercise E. Limit the amount of equipment required to complete the program

questions.explanation: A home programme must be individualised to the patient's needs.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: While talking to a patient about a previous exercise program, the patient mentions that he used to exclusively perform negative work. Negative work or a negative muscular contraction is best defined as:

options.A: The muscle develops tension and increases in length
options.B: The muscle develops tension and decrease in length
options.C: Muscle length remains constant as tension is develop

questions.explanation: Negative (eccentric) work is when the muscle develops tension while lengthening.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Jt. Structure and Function/Norkin/3rd Ed./Pg 99/

questions.question: The SAID principle stands for:

options.D: Specific amputation for impairment and disability

questions.explanation: SAID stands for Specific Adaptation to Imposed Demands.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Exercise causes heart rate to increase in linearity with increase in the physical effort. Maximum heart rate that can be attained during exercise is:
questions.explanation: Age-predicted maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 minus age.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist orders a wheelchair with a reclining back for a patient in a rehabilitation hospital. Which type of leg rests would be the most appropriate for the wheelchair? Physical Rehabilitation/Sullivan/5th Ed./Pg. 1305]
questions.explanation: A reclining-back wheelchair needs elevating leg rests to accommodate hip and knee extension.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist examines a patient for a standard wheelchair. The therapist measures from the patient's posterior buttock along the lateral thing to the popliteal fold. The therapist then subtracts two inches from the measurement. This method can be used to measure:
questions.explanation: Seat depth is the posterior buttock to popliteal fold distance minus 2 inches.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/Physical Rehabilitation/Sullivan/5th Ed/Pg. 1291

questions.question: Which manipulation is used to obtain sensory stimulation?
questions.explanation: Stroking is the manipulation used to give a sensory (soothing) stimulus.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: The Book of Massage Clair/Maxwell Hudson/ 1st Ed./Pg. 30

questions.question: In effleurage the hands move: Exercise Therapy

options.B: In the direction of lymph and venous flow from medial

questions.explanation: Effleurage strokes follow the direction of venous and lymph flow towards the heart.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Concise Exercise therapy/Roshan Lal Meena/1st Ed./Pg. 139

questions.question: A therapist designs a treatment plan for a patient with myositis ossificans. Which treatment would be contraindicated during the acute stage?
questions.explanation: Massage is contraindicated in the acute stage of myositis ossificans.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Transverse friction massage is a valuable treatment technique in a variety of common musculoskeletal disorders. Which of the fllowing statements does not accurately describe the application technique of transverse friction massage?

options.A: The therapist moves the skin back and forth in a direction perpendicular to the normal orientation of the fibers
options.B: A lubricant is used to prevent excessive skin friction
options.C: Fingers that are not involved directly in the massage are used to provide stabilization
options.D: The rate of movement is 2-3 cycles per second and rhythmical

questions.explanation: In deep transverse friction no lubricant is used so the skin moves with the fingers.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Concise Exercise Therapy/Roshan Lal Meena/ 1st Ed./Pg. 152

questions.question: Kneading, wringing, and rolling are all specific variations of which basic massage technique?
questions.explanation: Kneading, wringing and rolling are petrissage techniques.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter:
Cited reference: Concise Exercise Therapy/Peepee/Roshan Lal Meena/

1st Ed./Pg. 143

questions.question: Which type of joint receptor would a therapist expect to be most sensitive to high frequency vibration deep pressure, and velocity changes in joint position?

options.D: Ruffini endings Physiotherapy In Medical Condition

questions.explanation: Pacinian corpuscles respond to vibration, deep pressure and rapid changes in joint position.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter:
Cited reference: Physical Rehabilitation/O'sullivan/4th Ed./

Pg. 138-140

questions.question: A therapist attempts to obtain information on a patient's endurance level by administering a low level exercise test on a treadmill. Which of the following measurement methods would provide the therapist with an objective measurement of endurance?
questions.explanation: Rating of perceived exertion is an objective-scale measure of endurance during exercise testing.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Active repetitive exercises, usually of the ankles or wrist performed to maintain or improve circulation in the extremities are also known as:
questions.explanation: Pumping exercises of the ankles or wrists maintain circulation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Reliable method of increasing central excitation to stimulate motor units in largest proportion of muscle is by:

options.A: Application of assistance to voluntary movement
options.B: Application of resistance to voluntary movement

questions.explanation: Resistance to voluntary movement recruits the largest proportion of motor units.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist determines the maximum load patient can squat ten time is 240 lbs. The patient's ten repetition maximum should be recorded as:
questions.explanation: A 10-RM is the maximum load lifted ten times, here 240 lb.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient with unilateral lower extremity weakness. As the patient performs hip flexion in supine, the therapist helps the patient complete the full range of motion. This would best be described as:
questions.explanation: Helping the patient through the range is active-assisted exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The physician suggests that you start massage of a patient with back pain to reduce muscle spasms and assist in alleviating pain. The physician recommends that the massage you utilize consist of a series of brisk blows in alternating fashion. Of the following massages, which has the physician recommended?
questions.explanation: Tapotement (percussion) consists of brisk alternating blows such as hacking, clapping and pounding.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: You are working with a neurological patient and are concerned about promoting stability. You have to plan a treatment course that includes PNF patterns to increase and promote stability in this patient. What type of PNF pattern listed below would be most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Approximation promotes stability, while traction promotes mobility.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Principal of Exercise Therapy/Dena Gardiner/Pg. 83

questions.question: A patient is referred to the physical therapy department status post total hip replacement. The orders read "partial weightbearing utilizing a walker." Which of the following would be the most appropriate pattern given the above information?

options.A: Walker first, then involved lower extremity, then uninvolved extremity is advanced
options.B: Walker first, then one lower extremity, then the other lower extremity is advanced
options.C: Walker first, then uninvolved lower extremity, then involved lower extremity is advanced
options.D: Uninvolved extremity, then the walker, then the involved lower extremity is advanced

questions.explanation: For partial weight bearing with a walker, advance the walker, then the involved leg, then the uninvolved leg.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient is limited to 55 degrees in an active straight leg raise. A therapist should apply the contract-relax technique to the __________ to improve the patient's active range of motion?
questions.explanation: Contract-relax applied to the hamstrings and hip extensors improves limited straight leg raise.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient with a limited straight leg raise of 40 degrees due to inadequate hamstrings length. Which proprioceptive neuromuscular techniques would be most appropriate in increase the patient's hamstrings length?
questions.explanation: Contract-relax lengthens tight hamstrings.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist prepares to instruct a patient in a three-point gait pattern using axillary crutches. The most appropriate initial step to facilitate patient learning is to.

options.A: Distinguish a three-point gait pattern from other gait patterns
options.C: Provide the patient with direct feedback on his/her performance.
options.D: Provide a written handout which illustrates the use of a three-point gait pattern

questions.explanation: Demonstration is the best first step in teaching a crutch gait.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist treats a patient with quadriceps weakness using repeated contractions. This proprioceptive neuromascular facilitation technique should be applied:

options.B: At the point where the desired muscular response begin to diminish
options.C: At the end of the available range of motion
options.D: Only after a manual stretch to the hamstrings

questions.explanation: Repeated contractions are used at the point where the response begins to fade.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist instructs a patient in a D2 flexion pattern. Which of the following most accurately describes the scapula components of a D2 flexion pattern?
questions.explanation: The scapular component of D2 flexion is elevation, adduction and upward rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist uses proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation to increase join range of motion using the hold-relax technique. This technique utilizes an ______ contraction, which is at the end point of the available range of motion?
questions.explanation: Hold-relax uses an isometric contraction at the end of the available range.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist use proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation techniques to increase muscular strength. The therapist instructs the patient to actively perform a pattern of hip extension, abduction, and medial rotation. This pattern emphasizes strengthening of the:
questions.explanation: Hip extension, abduction and medial rotation emphasises the gluteal muscles.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Rhythmic stabilization is an ______ technique that can be implemented to increase join stability?
questions.explanation: Rhythmic stabilisation uses isometric contractions to increase stability.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist to improve a patient's lower extremity strength. Which proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation technique would be the most appropriate to achieve the therapist's goals?
questions.explanation: Repeated contractions are used to improve strength.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist designs an exercise program for a patient rehabilitating from a prolonged illness. Which of the following exercises is indicated for coordination training?
questions.explanation: Frenkel's exercises train coordination.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter:
Cited reference: Physical Rehabilitation/O'Sullivan/4th Ed./

Pg. 730-731

questions.question: A physical therapist treating a patient in supine elects to reinforce active movement of the lower extremity in a flexion, adduction, and lateral rotation pattern. This proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation technique pattern is termed:
questions.explanation: Lower limb flexion, adduction and lateral rotation is the D1 flexion pattern.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Cooling down exercises are performed for a period of:
questions.explanation: A cool-down lasts about 5 to 8 minutes.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: High intensity and high velocity resistance exercise characterized by a resisted eccentric muscle contraction followed by rapid concentric contraction followed by a rapid concentric contraction and designed to increase the muscle power and contraction is also known as:
questions.explanation: Plyometric training uses a rapid eccentric stretch followed by a rapid concentric contraction.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist instructs a patient to perform a quadriceps setting exercise. This exercise is considered to be an _________ exercise?
questions.explanation: Quadriceps setting is an isometric exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: What massage technique is commonly used at the beginning and conclusion of treatment and may be used during transitional periods prior to changing massage techniques?
questions.explanation: Effleurage is used at the beginning and end of a massage.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Concise Exercise therapy/Roshan Lal Meena/1st Ed./Pg. 139

questions.question: In axial suspension the fixed points lies:

options.A: Vertically above the joint requiring mobilization
options.B: Vertically above the joint proximal to the joint requiring mobilization
options.C: Vertically above the joint distal to the joint requiring mobilization

questions.explanation: In axial suspension the fixed point lies vertically above the joint being mobilised.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Concise Exercise Therapy/Roshan Lal Meena/1st Ed./Pg. 155

questions.question: A therapist examines a patient seated in a wheelchair. After completing the examination the therapist determines the wheelchair has inadequate seat width. Which of the following is the most likely consequences?

options.A: Excessive pressure under the distal thigh
options.B: Excessive pressure under the ischial tuberosities
options.C: Excessive pressure in the popliteal fossa
options.D: Excessive pressure on the greater trochanters

questions.explanation: A seat that is too narrow presses on the greater trochanters (and hips); a seat that is too wide causes poor posture and propulsion problems.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: An elderly patient with a minor right ankle inversion sprain is learning to use a straight cane. Which of the following instructions would be the most appropriate?

options.A: Hold the cane in the right hand, step left, then step right
options.B: Hold the cane in the left hand, step left, the step right
options.C: Hold the cane in the right hand, step right, then step left
options.D: Hold the cane in the left hand step right, then step left

questions.explanation: The cane is held in the hand opposite the affected leg and advanced together with the affected leg.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with a fractured right tibia who is partial weight bearing is referred to physical therapy for fitting and instruction with an assistive device. During the examination the physical therapist identifies poor lower extremity strength Ed.and coordination. Which assistive device would be most appropriate for the patient?
questions.explanation: A walker offers the widest base and most stability for a partial-weight-bearing patient with poor strength and coordination.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist instructs a woman with left unilateral lower extremity weakness to descend stairs. The most appropriate position for the therapist to guard the patient is:

options.A: In front of the patient toward the left side
options.B: In front of the patient toward the right side
options.C: Behind the patient toward the left side
options.D: Behind the patient toward the right side

questions.explanation: When a patient with left-sided weakness descends stairs, the therapist guards in front on the involved side.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist examines a 25 year old male rehabilitating from a tibial plateau fracture. The physician orders indicate the patient is non-weight bearing on the involved lower extremity. The most appropriate gait pattern for the patient is:
questions.explanation: A non-weight-bearing patient uses a three-point gait with the crutches and uninvolved leg.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist instructs a patient ambulating with axillary crutches to move cautiously and deliberately on any potentially hazardous surface. Which gait pattern would allow the patient maximum security?
questions.explanation: Four-point gait is the slowest, most stable crutch gait because three points of support are always on the ground.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist measures a patient for a straight cane prior to beginning ambulation activities. Which gross measurement method would provide the best estimate of cane length?

options.A: Measuring from the head of the fibula straight to the floor and multiplying by two
options.B: Measuring from the iliac crest straight to the floor
options.C: Measuring from the grate trochanter straight to the floor
options.D: Dividing the patient's height by two and adding three inches

questions.explanation: Cane length is estimated from the greater trochanter to the floor.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Roshan Meena concise/Exercise therapy/Pg. 77

questions.question: A therapist attempts to identify an appropriate gait pattern for a patient with bilateral lower extremity invol- vement due to muscle weakness. The patient presents with balance and coordination deficits. The most appropriate gait pattern using axillary crutches is:
questions.explanation: Four-point gait is used for bilateral weakness with balance and coordination problems.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient who is partial weight bearing on the left ambulates with a walker. The patient advances the walker followed by a step with the left and then a step with the right. This gait pattern is termed:
questions.explanation: Advancing the walker, then the affected leg, then the good leg is a three-point pattern.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient requires a walker for gait training. When fitting the walker for the patient the elbow should be place in:
questions.explanation: The walker is set so the elbows are flexed about 20-30 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Weakness in the ______ would make it extremely difficult to ambulate on crutches?
questions.explanation: Latissimus dorsi depresses the shoulder girdle and is essential for lifting the body on crutches.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Joint Structure and Function/Norkin/3rd Ed./Pg. 440

questions.question: A therapist instructs a patient diagnosed with multiple sclerosis to ambulate using two canes. Which gait pattern would be the most appropriate when using two canes?
questions.explanation: Two canes are used with a four-point alternate pattern.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with latissimus dorsi and lower trapezius weakness would have the most difficulty performing which of the following activities?

options.B: Modified two-point gait with a straight cane

questions.explanation: Swing-through gait needs strong shoulder depressors (latissimus dorsi, lower trapezius).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist is required to train a 71-year-old patient to ascend and descend a flight of stairs. The patient presents with a fractured left tibia and is weight bearing as tolerated. There is moderate weakness in the involved lower extremity secondary to the fracture. The most appropriate instruction are:

options.A: "One step at a time, right foot first to ascend and to ascend and to descend the stairs."
options.B: "One step at a time, right foot first to ascend the stairs and left foot first to descend the stairs."
options.D: "One step at a time left foot first to ascend and to descend the stairs."

questions.explanation: The rule is up with the good, down with the bad: ascend leading with the right, descend leading with the left.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Which assistive device allows for a two-point, threepoint, and four-point gait pattern?
questions.explanation: Axillary crutches allow two-, three- and four-point gaits.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient is referred to physical therapy for gait training following an extended illness. The patient has poor balance, but is able to move her legs alternately. Which of the following gait patterns would be the most stable?
questions.explanation: Four-point gait is the most stable pattern for poor balance.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist instructs a female athlete to complete ten minutes of stretching before beginning her treadmill program. While observing the athlete stretching her hamstring, the therapist notices repetitive bouncing and a failure to maintain the stretch for more than five seconds. Why is this type stretching considered to be inadequate?

options.A: The athlete should maintain each stretch for at least 30 seconds
options.B: The athlete should stretch only after running on the treadmill
options.C: The athlete is activating the stretch reflex
options.D: The athlete should remain activity specific and does not need to stretch the hamstrings if she is running on the treadmill

questions.explanation: Bouncing (ballistic) stretching triggers the stretch reflex, so the muscle contracts instead of relaxing.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
